text:
jia: quick check-in — I'm prototyping a split virtual pool where the global vpool is logically divided into GPU-local and host-backed subpools. goal is to reduce long-term fragmentation on GPU while keeping short-lived pages cheap to migrate. tradeoffs: migration throughput vs fragmentation debt across tenants. thoughts?

kevin: curious — what metrics do we care most for this? resident set fragmentation, page fault rate, p99 latency? also want numbers for hotset size distribution.

maria: +1 on measuring fragmentation + reclaim churn. in past experiments hard-partitioning cured cross-tenant thrash but created cold-evict churn when batch sizes spike. soft modes (hinted residency) worked better operationally.

jia: yeah — I'm leaning toward a 2-mode design: `soft-split` (residency hints + preferred allocation) and `hard-split` (strict allocation buckets). soft reduces migration IO but can leave more GPU-resident slack; hard minimizes fragmentation but needs strong admission.

sam: important: rolling upgrades. older hosts won't understand the split; need a negotiation during runtime handshake to fall back to single vpool. otherwise clients may assume guarantees that don't exist.

kevin: agree. also want a microbench plan: run synthetic workloads (seq=64/512/2048, batch sizes 1/8/32) and real traces (LLM chat replay) to see tail effects. add a churn test where many small contexts are created/dropped.

offload-bot: [auto] recent perf scan: baseline vpool shows 9-12% p99 token latency increase under 32-batch burst when host-backed pages > 40% of working set. trace: https://perf/redwood/trace/17887

maria: that matches memory-offload proto where host-backed >40% drove page fault storms. soft-split should keep hot prefixes pinned to GPU. also watch KVCACHE interactions — pinned KV pages shouldn't be evicted into host band.

jia: proposal sketch (config + runtime):
```
allocator:
  subpools:
    enabled: true
    mode: soft  # soft | hard
    heuristics:
      hot_threshold_ms: 120000
      migrate_on_hotburst: true
```
runtime handshake: `GET_FEATURES` returns `vpool.subpools=v1` fallback to legacy if absent.

kevin: can we keep single logical alloc API so higher layers are unchanged? under the hood allocator maps to subpool. we should surface minimal new ops: `hint_residency(addr, prefer_gpu|prefer_host)` for runtime callers.

maria: yep. keep API stable. we should add telemetry event names: `vpool.alloc.subpool`, `vpool.migrate.start`, `vpool.migrate.finish`, `vpool.fragmentation.sample`. acceptance: no API change for callers, opt-in config, metrics show fragmentation drop >= 15% in 30d sim.

sam: ops checklist:
- handshake fallback implemented
- config gating behind runtime flag
- migration backpressure (throttle concurrent page moves)
- safety net: if migration IO > X MB/s for Y sec, flip to soft-mode

jia: good list. question: migration policy — should we prefer migrating small pages first (reduce latency) or large contiguous ranges (improve compaction)? my intuition: prioritize contiguous ranges for long-term compaction, but allow opportunistic small-page moves when latency slack exists.

kevin: agree on hybrid. make policy pluggable and add simulation knobs. also run tenant-isolation test: two tenants, one heavy cold spilling, ensure other tenant's hotset isn't penalized.

maria: one more: eviction order must respect function-level hints (e.g., KV cache > model weights > temp activations). we already tag allocations but need consistent merge with subpool admission.

offload-bot: [auto] perf-run scheduled: 1788882500 -> job id 7a3c, will run 20k chat requests (seq 512) with soft/hard/legacy. will post results.

jia: action items: I will push a small PR adding the config + handshake signal and a simulator that models migration IO and fragmentation; kevin will own microbench plan; maria will enumerate acceptance telemetry and eviction ranking integration; sam will draft upgrade policy doc.

sam: thanks. please ping #release-war-room when handshake proto lands. :thumbsup:

kevin: SGTM — will add test matrix to the PR.

maria: thanks — will review and add KV cache edgecases.

jia: thanks all. I'll post a follow-up with the PR link and initial sim numbers.
